lesson.text: Quick memory: which buttons help when someone upsets you in this game? (MUTE, BLOCK and REPORT.) Today: the people you meet online.
Online, anyone can pick any name and any picture. Someone who says they are 11 might be a grown-up. You can't see who is really typing.
Keep your personal details private: your full name, where you live, your school, your phone number, your passwords, and photos that show any of them.
Warning signs: someone asks for secrets or photos, or offers gifts. They want to chat somewhere private, say 'don't tell your parents', or ask to meet you.
Worked example: a player asks what school you go to. You say you don't share that. When they ask for your address, you BLOCK them, REPORT them with ASKED SECRETS, and tell a trusted adult.

lesson.text: Never meet someone you only know online. If anyone asks you to, tell a trusted adult straight away. Telling is always right, and you are never in trouble for telling.
Most people online are kind, and playing together can be great fun. The rules keep you safe with everyone, so you never have to guess who is who.
Try it in the world: with a grown-up, find MUTE, BLOCK and REPORT in this game. Talk about who you would tell if something online worried you. Next: technology for everyone.

exercises.prompt: Someone online who says they are 11 might really be a grown-up.
exercises.hint: Can you see who is typing?
exercises.explain: True: anyone can type any age, name or picture, so you can't be sure who someone is.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: keep private, or OK to share in a game?
exercises.hint: Could it help someone find you, or get into your account?
exercises.explain: Your address, school and password stay private. A favourite colour or your buddy's name are fine.

exercises.prompt: A player you don't know asks where you live. What should you do?
exercises.hint: Is where you live a personal detail?
choices: Don't tell them, block them and tell an adult
Tell them if they seem nice
exercises.explain: Where you live stays private. Don't answer, BLOCK them and tell a trusted adult.

exercises.prompt: Match what happened to what to do.
exercises.hint: Think of the game's buttons and the grown-ups who can help.
exercises.explain: Mean words: MUTE or BLOCK. Secrets: REPORT and tell an adult. Asked to meet: tell a trusted adult. Kind: be kind back.

exercises.prompt: Which message is a warning sign?
exercises.hint: Which message asks for something private?
choices: send me a photo of you
exercises.explain: Asking for a photo of you is a warning sign: don't send one, and tell a trusted adult.

messages: send me a photo of you
picture.name: Builder99

exercises.prompt: Put these in order when someone online asks for your address.
exercises.hint: Keep yourself safe first, then get help.
exercises.explain: Don't answer, BLOCK them, REPORT them with ASKED SECRETS, and tell a trusted adult.

exercises.prompt: If you shared a secret online by mistake, it is too late to tell an adult.
exercises.explain: False: it is never too late. A trusted adult can help, and you are not in trouble.

exercises.prompt: Someone says: 'This is our secret, don't tell your parents.' What does that tell you?
exercises.hint: Why would someone kind want you to hide things from your family?
choices: It is a warning sign: tell a trusted adult
exercises.explain: Asking you to hide things from your parents is a warning sign. Tell a trusted adult.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: a warning sign, or OK?
items: asks you to chat in another app
offers free gold for your password
asks for a photo of you
asks to build together in the game
exercises.hint: Does it ask for something private, or try to get you somewhere private?
exercises.explain: Moving to another app, asking for your password or a photo are warning signs. Saying good game or building together in the game is OK.

exercises.prompt: A friendly player you have played with for weeks asks to meet at the park. What is safest?
exercises.hint: Do you really know who they are?
choices: Tell a trusted adult; never meet without one
Go with a friend your age
exercises.explain: You can't be sure who they are. Tell a trusted adult, and never meet someone from online without one.

exercises.prompt: Why can a profile picture of a child not prove that the player is a child?
exercises.explain: Anyone can choose any picture, even one copied from someone else, so it proves nothing about who is typing. The safety rules work whoever it is.

exercises.prompt: It is your fault if someone online tricks you.
exercises.hint: Who is doing something wrong: the trickster, or you?
exercises.explain: False: it is never your fault. People who trick children work hard to seem friendly. Tell a trusted adult, and they will help.

exercises.prompt: Which username gives away too much?
exercises.hint: Does the name tell a stranger anything about where you live or how old you are?
exercises.explain: Tilly_Oak_Street_11 gives away her name, her street and her age: three clues to finding her. StarBuilder, BlueBuddyFan and CastleMaker give nothing away.

exercises.prompt: Juno reported a player and told her dad. What happens to her?
exercises.hint: Is telling a grown-up the right thing to do?
choices: She did the right thing and is not in trouble
She must stop playing for ever
exercises.explain: Reporting and telling a trusted adult is exactly right, and Juno is not in trouble. Her dad can help, and her report can stop the player upsetting other children too.

exercises.prompt: Sort the usernames: safe, or gives away too much?
exercises.hint: Look for a real name, a town, a school, a birth year or an age.
exercises.explain: Safe: StarBuilder, BlueBuddyFan and CastleMaker tell a stranger nothing. Too much: a full name and town, a birth year and school, and an age and city could help someone find you.
